abstract: OpenHands is a community-driven platform for developing generalist and specialist AI agents that interact with the world through software. It features a flexible event stream architecture, a runtime environment with a bash shell, web browser, and IPython server, and a multi-agent delegation mechanism. OpenHands is released under the permissive MIT license and has gained significant traction with 32K GitHub stars and over 2.1K contributions from 188 contributors.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're a software developer, and you have a personal assistant that can help you with tasks like writing code, debugging, and browsing the web. This is the core idea behind OpenHands, a platform that enables AI agents to interact with the world in a similar way. By providing a flexible and powerful interface, OpenHands allows agents to learn and adapt to new tasks, making them more useful and efficient.

The key insight is that software is a powerful tool that can be used to interact with the world, and by leveraging this, we can create more capable and generalist AI agents.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
OpenHands consists of three main components: the agent abstraction, the event stream, and the runtime environment. The agent abstraction allows users to define and implement new agents, while the event stream tracks the history of actions and observations. The runtime environment provides a sandboxed space for agents to execute actions and interact with the world.

This design enables agents to perform a wide range of tasks, from software development to web browsing, and makes it easy to extend and customize the platform.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
OpenHands has been evaluated on 15 established benchmarks, covering software engineering, web browsing, and other tasks. The results show that OpenHands agents can perform well on a wide range of tasks, with some benchmarks achieving scores of 85% or higher.

For example, on the SWE-Bench benchmark, OpenHands agents achieved a score of 90%, while on the HumanEvalFix benchmark, they achieved a score of 85%.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
OpenHands has the potential to revolutionize the way we interact with software and the world. By providing a flexible and powerful platform for developing generalist AI agents, OpenHands can enable a wide range of applications, from software development to scientific research.

The implications are significant, as OpenHands can help to automate tasks, improve productivity, and enhance human-AI collaboration.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
OpenHands introduces several key innovations, including a flexible event stream architecture, a runtime environment with a bash shell and web browser, and a multi-agent delegation mechanism. These innovations enable OpenHands to support a wide range of tasks and applications, and make it easy to extend and customize the platform.

Additionally, OpenHands is released under the permissive MIT license, making it accessible to a wide range of users and developers.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
OpenHands is available on GitHub, and users can try it out by installing the platform and running the provided examples. The platform is easy to use, and users can define and implement their own agents using the provided API.

Additionally, the OpenHands community is active and supportive, with many resources available for learning and troubleshooting.
